title: Anthropic says it cut Claude reasoning token theft by up to 99% in fight against industrial-scale distillation
key_facts: Anthropic says its new defenses have cut the volume of extracted reasoning tokens (the model's internal chain-of-thought steps) by 90 to 99 percent.
In distillation attacks, companies systematically copy an AI model's capabilities to train their own smaller models; attackers use networks of hundreds of thousands of fake accounts.
Anthropic names the Chinese companies Zhipu and Moonshot as participants.
Zhipu allegedly siphoned cyber capabilities from leading US models for its GLM-5.3 model; Moonshot secretly routed queries through Claude.
The report says the copied capabilities could end up in foreign military and surveillance systems.
Anthropic now restricts access to Claude's internal reasoning steps, runs a classifier that detects extraction attempts and automatically bans flagged accounts; tens of thousands have been banned.
Anthropic is calling on other AI developers to adopt similar protections and admits legitimate users are being caught up in the process too.
